newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FORECAST - Taiwan March M2 seen up 10.03 pct y/y.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Taiwan March M2 seen up 10.03 pct y/y.

text.p: A Reuters poll of Taiwan economists projected an average 10.03 percent year-on-year growth for Taiwan's broadest M2 money supply in March.
The figures are due to be released by the central bank at about 0410 GMT on April 25.
February's M2 money supply growth was 9.88 percent
year-on-year.
Institution March growth (yr/yr)
HSBC James Capel 9.65
National Securities 10.0
Nikko Securities 10.5
Nomura Securities 9.95
Average 10.03
Economists said they expected March M2 growth to fall into the central bank's target zone of 9-14 percent growth for the third straight month since it adopted a new definition of M2 in January.
They estimated the new definition would add some 1.0 to 1.5 percentage points to previous M2 growth.
Economists noted slowly increasing money demand, although most of that flooded into the growing stock market.
"We haven't seen strong investment-triggered money demand as the economic recovery is still in its early stage," said Nomura Securities economist Amy Huang.
The central bank's repeated issuance of negotiable certificates of deposits to mop up excess liquidity in the banking system should limit M2 growth, economists said.
"The central bank's NCD issue, widely seen to cool off the rallying stock market, would offset March's M2 growth," said HSBC James Capel economist Stephen Wang.
At one point in mid-April the Taiwan share index had risen about 25 percent during 1997 but has since declined a little.
The central bank's previous definition of money supply was: M1A equalled cash, checking accounts and passbook deposits. M1B was M1A plus savings accounts. M2 was M1B plus quasi-money.

The bank said it would stick to its M1A and M1B definition, while M2 was revised to M1B plus time deposits, foreign currency deposits, postal funds, repurchase agreement trade outstanding and foreigners' Taiwan dollar holdings.

The new M2 definition uses the post offices' total deposit amount instead of postal offices' redeposits in banks, adds repurchase agreement trade outstanding and foreigners' Taiwan dollar holdings. It deletes the net value of financial bonds, savings bonds and treasury bills and foreign-currency trust funds, the bank said in a statement.
-- Taipei Newsroom (2-5080815)
